dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise, how can I help you this afternoon?
Hi Denise. I'm calling to report that the ocean moved into my mother's basement this weekend and didn't pay rent. Not totally joking, unfortunately.
Oh no. From the storm Friday into Saturday?
Yeah. So, my name's Daniel Haddad, the house is my mom's, Priya Haddad. Six Brewer Street, Fifth Ward, right on the corner there.
Six Brewer Street. Okay, I've got it up. Tell me what happened.

So overnight Friday into Saturday, the tenth, the storm drain on the corner backed right up. Water came up out of the grate first, my mother saw it, it was bubbling up out of the street like a fountain, and then it ran across the sidewalk and started coming in the house. Through the seam in the foundation wall, the corner side, the side that faces the drain.
How much water are we talking about in the basement?

About four inches. It's not finished down there, thank God, it's just a concrete floor. But the dehumidifier was sitting in it, that's dead now. The shelving's all wet, and the holiday decorations, which they just put away, were on the bottom shelves in cardboard boxes. So that's mush.
I'm sorry. That's a mess to come home to.

Yeah. And look, I'll be honest with you, the part that gets me is that grate. It's been packed with leaves since, I don't know, November? You can see it from the sidewalk. Nobody ever came by. Every time I'm over there I'm out kicking leaves off it myself. And then a real storm hits and of course it can't take the water, and it comes straight into my mother's house. Like, that's the city's drain. That's not something she can fix.
No, I understand. That's exactly what we want to hear about, so I'm glad you called. Is the drain still backed up now, today, or did it go down?

It went down Saturday afternoon. But it's still slow. I was over there yesterday and there's still a puddle sitting around it, and there's junk on top of the grate. Leaves, there's like a plastic bag in there.
Okay. I'm putting this in as a drain backup at the corner by six Brewer, water came into the basement, about four inches, entering at the foundation on the corner side. Sound right?
That's right.
I can get a crew to check that corner tomorrow, Tuesday. They're running all over town after the weekend, so it'll be sometime during the day, not a set hour.

Tomorrow's fine. I'd rather tomorrow than whenever. But can I ask, when they come, is that just going to be somebody pulling the leaves off the top? Because that's what I've been doing for two months, and it obviously doesn't cut it if the water's coming up out of it.
I'll put a note on it that the grate's been clogged for a while and it backed up into the house, so they know to look at more than the top. If they find something further down, they'll write it up.

Okay. Good. Put that in, please. The other thing, and I don't know if this is even a thing you guys do. Next time there's a big one coming, could the city put a pump truck on that corner? Just park it there and keep the water down? Because my mother and Leila, they're the ones in the house, they can't be out there at two in the morning with a broom and buckets.

That I don't know the answer to off the top of my head. I'll put the request in the notes so the supervisor sees it with the work order. I'd rather they tell you yes or no than me making something up.
Fair enough. I just want somebody to actually think about it before the next one, not after.
Understood. What's a good number for you, in case they need to reach somebody?
My cell, 401-555-0172. Call me, not the house. I'd rather deal with it.
401-555-0172, Daniel Haddad. Got it.
And honestly, thank you for picking up. I almost filled out the thing on the website and a buddy of mine said don't bother, just call and talk to an actual person, you'll get further. So here I am.
Well, tell your buddy thanks. The website goes to us too, but I get it, sometimes you want to hear somebody say it back to you.
Exactly. Okay. So tomorrow, crew looks at the corner, and the pump truck thing goes to the supervisor.
That's it. If they don't show tomorrow, call back and ask for me, Denise, and I'll chase it down.
I'll hold you to that. Thanks, Denise.
You're welcome. I hope the basement dries out. Take care.
